description: Deprecated bank of eight voltage controlled clock dividers, kept only so that old patches go on loading; its browser name says do not use it, and Polyrhythmic Generator MkII replaces it

params.text: Scales the voltage at that channel's division CV input, from -100% at one end through nothing at the centre to +100% at the other
Sets that channel's division by hand across a range of 0 to 10
Silences that channel's output, and its share of the polyphonic output, while it is engaged
Mutes every channel at once while it is engaged
Engaged, a channel pulses on the first count after a reset and every N clocks after that; released, its first pulse comes only after half the division has been counted, and every N clocks after that
Sets what every channel output carries: T a trigger every Nth clock, G a gate high for N clocks then low for N, GC the clock passed for N clocks then muted for N, and C one clock pulse every N

inputs.text: The clock for that channel; with nothing patched it takes the clock from the channel above, so one cable at the top clocks every channel below it
A rising edge restarts that channel's count; with nothing patched it takes the reset from the channel above, so one cable at the top resets every channel below it
Voltage that shifts that channel's division, added to the division knob once the CV amount knob has scaled it; with nothing patched it takes the voltage from the channel above
A high gate mutes every channel at once
A high gate here keeps the module counting; the button does that by hand

outputs.text: Carries that channel's divided clock in whichever form the output mode switch has chosen
The eight channels gathered into one polyphonic cable, channel 1 to 8 in order

notes: this version divides by 2, 4, 6, 8 and so on rather than by 1, 2, 3, 4; the MkII module set to Legacy Mode reproduces that behaviour
